name: enqueue
description: A graph whose root names a queue for its commits and one for its releases: on the generated tables, which are Postgres's, each commit written, a change set's and a merge's alike, enqueues the commit queue's message with its root, ref, commit and sequence, null on a commit that is not tagged; a root's first release and each move of it to another commit enqueue the release queue's message, and a release of the commit already released does not. The fixed layout has no trigger, so its steps read no queue.

statement.postgres: SELECT count(*)::text AS messages FROM recipe_committed_queue WHERE root = $1::uuid

SELECT CASE "commit" WHEN $2::uuid THEN 'd1' WHEN $3::uuid THEN 'c1' ELSE 'other' END AS "commit", CASE ref WHEN $4::uuid THEN 'write' WHEN $5::uuid THEN 'main' ELSE 'other' END AS ref, COALESCE("sequence"::text, 'none') AS "sequence", state FROM recipe_committed_queue WHERE root = $1::uuid ORDER BY created_at, "sequence" NULLS FIRST
SELECT count(*)::text AS messages FROM recipe_published_queue WHERE root = $1::uuid
SELECT CASE "commit" WHEN $2::uuid THEN 'c1' ELSE 'other' END AS "commit" FROM recipe_published_queue WHERE root = $1::uuid ORDER BY created_at
SELECT CASE "commit" WHEN $2::uuid THEN 'c1' WHEN $3::uuid THEN 'c2' ELSE 'other' END AS "commit" FROM recipe_published_queue WHERE root = $1::uuid ORDER BY created_at
SELECT count(*)::text AS messages FROM recipe_committed_queue WHERE root = $1::uuid
